data.claim: api/gates.run builds gdef from load_gates(repo=PRIMARY) (the primary's .ddflow/config.toml + gates.toml + local layer) and passes it to run_command_gate(gdef, cwd=item worktree), which runs it against the branch's own pyproject/uv.lock. run_command_gate knows cwd, so it can read the TREE's committed gate table and the primary's (infra.worktree.repo_root(cwd)) itself and compare the execution fields when the command fails.
data.falsifier: If run_command_gate were passed a gdef built from the tree, or api/gates reloaded gates per worktree, there would be no drift; grep shows load_gates(repo, cfg) at api/gates.py:103 and _resolve, run_command_gate(gdef, cwd) at api/gates.py:326.
data.mechanism: load_gates(root) reads tomlcfg.config_paths(root); committed layers are [:2]; the local layer is git-ignored and exists only in the primary, so only committed layers can be compared tree-vs-primary.
data.probe: grep -n 'load_gates(\|run_command_gate(' ddflow/api/gates.py; sed -n 311,358p ddflow/services/gates.py; sed -n 106,120p ddflow/infra/worktree.py
data.probe_output: load_gates(repo, cfg) at 77,103 (+_resolve); run_command_gate(gdef, cwd, ...) at 326 with cwd from _where_to_run -> _item_tree; repo_root uses --git-common-dir
data.question: Where does a command gate's definition come from vs where does it run, and where can drift be detected within ddflow/services/gates.py?

evidence.note: R-gate-config-drift CONFIRMED: gdef from load_gates(primary) at api/gates.py:103, run_command_gate(gdef, cwd=item tree) at :326; tree has its own committed gate table to compare

brief --item + recall: D-failed-critic-not-blocking; L-gate-cmd-vs-branch-deps (merge main before unit_tests after a gate-config change: the manual workaround this fix automates the diagnosis of); L1907ee4695; R-config-forward-compat (reuse its 'config is newer than this code: merge main' vocabulary)

run_command_gate: a FAILED run is checked for gate-config drift (primary vs tree, run fields only). behind (base committed a new definition since the fork, tree carries the forked one) -> unavailable 'your branch is behind a gate-config change on <base>: ... merge <base> into this branch, then re-run'; own (branch changed it) -> failed, naming the command that ran; primary-uncommitted -> no drift. tests/test_gate_config_drift.py 6 tests; regression fails on unfixed code (revert-checked); full suite 2609 passed

data.summary: gate_config_drift classifies from working trees: an uncommitted gate edit in the primary on top of a committed gate change hides the 'behind' drift (bare test failure again), and an uncommitted gate edit in the item tree mislabels a behind branch as 'own'. Found by critic review of B-fix-gate-config-drift. Fix: classify on committed specs (tree HEAD vs fork vs primary HEAD).

review.split_diff: a single file bigger than the chunk budget yields a HEADER-ONLY chunk (the newline after the header counts as a 'hunk', so the first real hunk overflows and flushes the bare header) and the next chunk glues the hunk header onto the '+++ b/<file>' line ('+++ b/t.py@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@'). The reviewer then reports the new file as EMPTY: both DeepSeek reviews of B-fix-gate-config-drift raised HIGH/MEDIUM 'tests/test_gate_config_drift.py is an empty file' findings and recorded rubber_duck/critic failed. Probe: split_diff('diff --git a/t.py b/t.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/t.py
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
' + 50 lines, 400) -> first piece is the 71-char header alone. Root: header = f.split('
@@',1)[0] drops the '
' into the hunk list.

gate_config_drift compares committed layers only, but load_gates also merges the git-ignored .ddflow/local layer: when the local layer overrides a run field (e.g. command) the command that RAN is the local one, yet a committed change on main vs an older branch was reported as 'behind' and a genuine failure recorded unavailable. Found by rubber_duck review. Fix: overlay the primary's local layer on every spec compared.

gate_config_drift checks 'own' before 'behind': a branch that committed any run-field edit (e.g. timeout_s) and is ALSO behind a committed command change on main is labelled 'own' and recorded as a bare test FAILURE of main's command -- the original B8ea7a90aea symptom. Found by rubber_duck review. Fix: a base change since the fork is 'behind' first.

data.rule: When ddflow review reports a newly added file as empty or hunk-less, check the file exists with content and treat the finding as the split_diff header-only-chunk artefact (bug B-split-diff-header-chunk) until that is fixed.
data.title: A review finding that a new file is empty is the chunker, not the diff
data.why: Three DeepSeek reviews of B-fix-gate-config-drift each raised a HIGH 'tests/test_gate_config_drift.py is empty' finding; split_diff sends the file header alone in one chunk when the file exceeds the budget.
